items.headline: Trump AI cybersecurity executive order (voluntary frontier-model framework)
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's AI-governance story was the congressional Great American AI Act discussion draft (Obernolte/Trahan, three-year state preemption). Today the focus shifts to the executive branch: the analysis of Trump's June 2 "Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security" order, which yesterday's news did not cover. The new substance is what outside counsel now read into the text — a cybersecurity-centered order (CISA hardening directives, an AI Cybersecurity Clearinghouse, a 60-day frontier-model benchmarking track with a strictly voluntary up-to-30-day pre-release access option) that explicitly bars mandatory licensing or preclearance. The EO is framed as the executive-branch counterpart to the congressional debate carried yesterday, making it a distinct artifact rather than a continuation of the Great American AI Act bullet.

items.headline: Flowise MCP RCE (CVE-2026-40933, CVSS 9.9)
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's agentic-security item was the Langroid prompt-to-SQL flaw (CVE-2026-25879, CVSS 9.8) in its SQLChatAgent. Today is a different CVE on a different vector: CVE-2026-40933 is an OS command-injection RCE in Flowise's Model Context Protocol stdio adapter, where a one-click chatflow import can trigger execution; fixed in Flowise 3.1.0. It is a separate advisory, not a fresh state-change on the Langroid one. The new angle is the disclosure debate — Obsidian Security's proof-of-concept and its argument that the allowlist patch treats the symptom rather than the cause, recommending operators drop stdio for Server-Sent Events — which reframes the underlying through-line from text-to-SQL injection (yesterday) to the MCP stdio transport as an actively probed attack surface.

items.headline: China Renaissance initiates Nvidia at Buy, $319 target
items.diff_narrative: Absent from yesterday's brief, whose markets/model item was MiniMax M3's open-weight launch claim. Today introduces a fresh sell-side action: China Renaissance opened Nvidia coverage on June 5 at Buy with a $319 target, a new desk added to the roster and a target well above the prior week's Needham $270. The signal worth tracking — a China-focused shop initiating at Buy rather than flagging export or demand risk — is new today and was not part of yesterday's coverage.

Fresh changes versus yesterday: WWDC26 has moved from a calendar listing to an imminent catalyst opening this coming Monday June 8; The AI Summit London (Tobacco Dock, June 10-11) is a newly added named entrant for the mid-June window; the Databricks keynote detail is sharpened to a specific cross-vendor lineup (Ghodsi, Zaharia, Brockman, Chase, Moura); and the Zenity expansion is restated with dates still unpublished and flagged for monitoring.
